narrative.overview: Spctre is a product interface for people making accountable policy decisions. The system should feel like an operational ledger: restrained, dense, traceable, and legible under review pressure. It shows confidence by making provenance visible, not by adding spectacle.
keyCharacteristics: Provenance visible in branch IDs, revision IDs, hashes, runtime targets, and policy refs.
Flat surfaces with tonal layering instead of shadow theatrics.
Status is always textual as well as chromatic.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ledger Teal is the only product accent. Do not introduce purple, blue, or neon AI gradients.

rules.name: The Status Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Amber, red, and green are reserved for workflow state. Do not use semantic colors as decoration.

rules.name: The Metadata Is Product Rule
rules.body: IDs, hashes, policy refs, and timestamps must stay readable. Never hide them behind tooltips as the only access path.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Panels, rows, and cards do not cast shadows. If a surface needs emphasis, use hierarchy, semantic color, or content priority.

dos: Do keep product surfaces dense, compact, and operational.
Do expose branch IDs, revision IDs, artifact hashes, runtime targets, policy refs, approvers, and timestamps directly in the UI.
Do use Ledger Teal sparingly for primary actions, icons, and active identity.
Do reserve amber, red, and green for real workflow status.
Do prefer full borders, tonal fills, and icon-led rows for emphasis.
Do keep cards and panels at 8px radius or less.
Do keep text at fixed, readable sizes rather than scaling with viewport width.
donts: Don't make Spctre feel like an Azure-only governance dashboard.
Don't use generic AI gradients, purple-blue glow effects, or glassmorphism.
Don't turn the control plane into a marketing-heavy SaaS shell.
Don't hide provenance behind vague copy such as policy updated when the branch, revision, and hash are available.
Don't use thick colored side stripes on cards, rows, callouts, or alerts.
Don't use oversized hero typography, floating orb backgrounds, or decorative metrics.
Don't introduce shadows as a default surface treatment.
